claims.text: Spin-polarized density functional theory can predict ferromagnetic ground states.
The proposed method applies where electron exchange and correlation effects are critical.
The material is initially in a high-symmetry non-magnetic or paramagnetic phase.
Ground-state magnetic ordering can be assessed by comparing energies obtained from spin-polarized DFT calculations.
An appropriate exchange-correlation functional is required for the proposed calculation.
The calculations are to represent low temperature, zero external magnetic field, ideal periodic boundary conditions, and a well-converged basis set.
Crystal-lattice structure and electron-density distribution mediate the balance between kinetic and exchange-interaction energies.
Spin-polarized DFT treats electron exchange interactions that can stabilize a ferromagnetic state.
If aligned spins lower the total energy, the ferromagnetic state is energetically favored.
A predicted ferromagnetic ground state will have lower total energy than non-magnetic and alternative magnetic states.
A predicted ferromagnetic state will exhibit a finite computed magnetic moment.
Non-spin-polarized DFT provides a baseline for comparison.
The approach is most applicable to materials with localized electrons and dominant exchange effects.
The approach may be less reliable for itinerant magnetic systems unless additional many-body corrections are used.
Prediction accuracy depends on the exchange-correlation functional and treatment of electron correlation.
Benchmarking against experimental data is needed.
Failure to obtain both a lower ferromagnetic-state energy and a finite magnetic moment would falsify the hypothesis.
